test_frameworks.name: dbt tests
test_frameworks.scope: Generic tests in _*.yml, singular tests in transformation/tests/, unit tests in models/intermediate/_unit_tests.yml.

test_frameworks.name: pytest
test_frameworks.scope: Offline unit tests for ingestion, orchestration, and the two maps.

applications.name: nyc-taxi-duckdb-demo
applications.description: NYC taxi analytics over real TLC trip records for 2024-01 to 2024-03, plus two simulated source systems (fleet operations and master data). Warehouse file: domain.duckdb at the repo root.

bronze.notes: TLC trips and zone lookup, verbatim.

seeds.notes: Analyst-owned banding tables, loaded by dbt seed into their own schema; internal, like staging.

semantic_exclusions.reason: Not a star member: a HAVING floor keeps only well-populated origin-destination pairs (ADR 0017), so it is a filtered population, not the full set of trips; a model over it would mislead.
Unpivot of fare components into one row per component: summing its measures across trips fans out, so it cannot be a fact in a star.
No join key into any star: no fact carries a fare-regime key, so it cannot be a conformed dimension.

Its population is not statable from the trips dataset's own fields: it is billable trips whose pickup and dropoff zones are both in an NYC borough, and borough membership lives in dim_zone, not on the fact, so no content_filter can declare the subset. Its outbound_cross_borough_share also divides by its origin month's trips, so it is not additive across rows. ADR 0018 publishes the complete 5 x 5 grid with no trip floor, so the table is a filtered population and a repeating denominator rather than an aggregate source.

tlc.description: NYC TLC yellow and green trips and the zone lookup, fetched from the public TLC site.

ops.description: Fleet operator's platform, generated from the yellow trips.

mdm.description: Master-data platform: zones, vendors, payment methods, rate plans, regimes, boroughs, points of interest, calendar, weather.

run_ingest.notes: Starts the three pipelines serially, in the order its own PIPELINES list gives, and stops at the first failure.

ingestion.description: dlt pipelines (one per source), their source code under sources/, resource docs under docs/, and .dlt/config.toml.

orchestration.description: Scripts that run ingestion and the dbt build, in order.

staging.description: Views: one per source table, renamed and typed. Also holds _sources.yml.

intermediate.description: Business logic and joins: conformed trips, enrichment, fare components, quality flags, status intervals, shift occupancy and economics. Unit tests in _unit_tests.yml.

finance.description: Revenue marts. Apply the billable rule (ADR 0003): filter on `fct_trip.is_billable`, inside the report window.

ops.description: Fleet-operations marts: driver scorecard, vehicle utilisation, trip quality scorecard.

macros.description: trip_natural_key (the only definition of trip_key), report window, schema naming, finance helpers, and relations.sql, which renders ref() and source() without a catalog so stored views work in the renamed sandbox copy.

python_tests.description: pytest tests for ingestion, orchestration and the two maps.

decisions.description: ADRs, including the standing business answers.

designs.description: Design records per model and pipeline.

requirements.description: Requirements, one file per intent at artifact_paths.requirement; plans and verifications go to artifact_paths.plan and artifact_paths.verification when first written.

conventions.description: Operator conventions as skills (OpenHands lists each one): naming, style, testing, dlt, and what goes in context, ADRs and design records.

setup.description: Repo maintenance documents (requirements, work plan, conventions inventory, skill changes, data provenance). Not for ingestion or transformation tasks; not maintained by build agents.

reviews.description: Review outputs (onboarding, security, performance and others) whose findings are triaged: intent, proposal, declined or deferred.

proposals.description: Optional proposals for major functional or design items that need discussion before they become intents.

logical_model.description: Canonical semantic model, Apache Ossie 0.2.0.dev0: documents partition the model by whole fact stars (a star never straddles documents; a document may hold several), with shared dimensions copied per document and structure drift-checked. Authored under the semantic-model skill and reviewed under the validating-semantic-model skill; consumer formats export on the fly and are never committed.

ontology.description: Business ontology, Apache Ossie 0.2.0.dev0: the CONTEXT.md vocabulary as entity and value types with their relationships, plus one mapping per canonical document that concepts reach. Authored under the ontology skill and gated by validating-ontology (its own step: structure, then coverage, then content). Declarations only: nothing parses or executes a mapping.

contracts.description: ODCS v3.2.0 data contracts at `{schema}/{table}.odcs.yaml`, for the relations ADR-0225 puts under contract: the bronze and raw source tables and the gold relations. Staging, intermediate and seed models carry no contract; dbt `contract: enforced` on them is hand-kept in their properties files. Authored with the data-contract skill, drafted by `odcs.py reverse`, and gated by `odcs.py check`: the schema, the structure, agreement with the canonical document that names a gold relation, and its own generated dbt keys and dlt hints. The contract is the authored artifact; the enforcement generated from it is not.

key_directories.docs/setup/: Repo maintenance: how this repo was built, its decisions, the data-provenance notes, the skill changes it implies and the script that seeds the Studio Domain database. Not for ingestion or transformation tasks; do not read it for them, and do not maintain it.
key_directories.docs/review/: Review findings for triage. Not read during build tasks.
key_directories.docs/proposal/: Proposals that become intents. Read one only when the intent links to it.
key_directories.contracts/: ODCS data contracts for the relations ADR-0225 puts under contract (sources and gold). Read one before changing the relation it names.

notes_for_agents.startup: Read this file first. AGENTS.md says how to work; the skills in .agents/skills/ hold the conventions.
notes_for_agents.reporting_window: report_start and report_end are dbt vars in dbt_project.yml and define the business reporting window. They are not a sampling control.
notes_for_agents.synthetic_data: ops_raw and mdm_raw are simulated. TLC trips are real.
notes_for_agents.trip_key: Produced only by the trip_natural_key macro. The operator source carries natural columns, not the key.
notes_for_agents.warehouse: domain.duckdb at the repo root is ignored by git and rebuilt by orchestration/run_all.py.
notes_for_agents.dlt_environment: Pipelines need VD_DOMAIN_DATA_PLATFORM=duckdb_local, VD_DOMAIN_SECRET_STORE_KIND=local_toml and VD_EPHM_DUCKDB_LOCAL_PATH; orchestration/run_ingest.py sets them.
notes_for_agents.new_source: A new source mirrors an existing entry in `sources`: create every artifact it lists (module, config section, pipeline, resource docs, tests, design record). Mirror `tlc` for a downloaded file source. Add it to its runner's `orchestrators.<name>.runs` and to that runner's own code. When two sources share a `dataset`, each also declares `produces` (the tables it lands). Add it to `test-map.json` only when it needs its own test module.
notes_for_agents.setup_docs: docs/setup/ is repo maintenance. Do not read or maintain it for ingestion or transformation work.
notes_for_agents.reviews_and_proposals: docs/review/ holds review findings for triage; do not read it for build tasks. Read a docs/proposal/ file only when the intent's requirement links to it.
notes_for_agents.dbt_sources: dbt sources name a schema and never a database: the Studio sandbox is a renamed copy of the Domain file, so a catalog name never resolves there. dbt runs use the dev target.
notes_for_agents.artifact_paths: Every artifact location is declared here: requirement, plan, verification and case_record per intent, design records per model or pipeline (layered: design_record_model) or area. The plugin names an intent's artifacts; this map places them.
